sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cold-Chain Keg Wholesale and Export of Artisanal Hazy IPAs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French civil tradition with Belgian-inspired commercial law; unitary national legal system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.-Luxembourg Income Tax Convention, signed 3 April 1996, as amended by Protocol of 20 May 2009
Germany-Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement, signed 23 April 2012
France-Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement, signed 1 April 1958, as amended
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties with third countries
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, in force since 1 February 2019
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI), in force for Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended by the Law of 15 July 2021; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Art. 710-1 et seq. governing the SARL); Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; EU Regulation 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the country of origin (police, notary, or consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Apostille Convention OR consular legalization at a Luxembourg embassy for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade/corporate registry of the country of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary and local counsel, executed by each incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator(s) or authorized signatory of the corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association or equivalent constitutive document of any corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of commerce of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing the source of funds of the minimum share capital (EUR 12,000) and initial working capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: KYC-compliant financial institution of the shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarized; apostille not required for the bank letter itself

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif) and consent to appear in the RBE register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO, executed before the Luxembourg notary or a competent foreign authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatures executed outside Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against: (1) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulations 881/2002, 2580/2001, and 269/2014); (2) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) the OFAC SDN List and OFAC sectoral sanctions; (4) the Luxembourg national targeted financial sanctions list published by the Ministry of Finance; (5) the FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction lists; and (6) PEP and adverse-media databases (e.g., World-Check, LexisNexis Diligence) covering both domestic Luxembourg public offices and foreign PEPs under FATF Recommendations 12, 22, and 24. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered at 25% or greater UBO ownership, PEP status, high-risk geography, or any anomaly in the source of funds. Under AML/CFT Law Art. 3(2), the filing professional must perform ongoing monitoring and retain KYC records for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); available at https://www.lbr.lu (electronic filing via the LBR e-filing portal using a Luxembourg e-ID, Luxtrust, or EU eIDAS certificate)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All submissions to the RCS must be in one of Luxembourg's administrative languages (French, German, or Luxembourgish). The corporate name may be selected in any language written in Latin script; a compulsory transliteration is required for names originating in non-Latin scripts. Under Art. 710-1(1) of the Law of 10 August 1915, the SARL's name must be immediately followed by the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered name, must not be misleading as to the legal form or the corporate object, and must not infringe third-party trademarks or protected appellations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'State', 'Grand-Ducal', 'National', 'Government', 'Ministry', 'Public', 'Commune', 'Police' — terms implying state, municipal, or public institutional patronage; requires prior Grand-Ducal or ministerial approval
'Bank', 'Banque', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Financial Institution', 'Asset Management' — reserved for CSSF/ECB-licensed regulated entities; prior CSSF authorization mandatory
'SICAV', 'SICAF', 'FCP', 'Investment Fund', 'Fonds d'Investissement' — subject to CSSF supervision and prior authorization
'Société Anonyme', 'SA', 'SCA', 'SCS', 'Société en Commandite' — misleading as to the legal form of the SARL
'University', 'Université', 'Foundation', 'Fondation', 'Charity' — reserved for authorized educational or philanthropic institutions
'Luxembourg', 'European Union', 'EU', 'NATO', 'IMF', 'World Bank' — implying official sponsorship, state patronage, or international institutional affiliation
Geographical indications or protected designations of origin (e.g., EU Regulation 1151/2012) for beer and foodstuff names, where the company does not hold the corresponding certification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg operates a notary-mediated name clearance rather than a standalone reservation database; the notary verifies availability at the RCS and the exclusivity is provisional for 30 calendar days pending execution of the incorporation deed. Upon RCS rejection: (1) the notary submits a reasoned reconsideration request (constat) to the LBR within 10 business days; (2) if the refusal is upheld, the founders may apply to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement, commercial chamber) within two months of notification, requesting judicial overruling of the refusal; (3) where the refusal results from a ministerial decision on sensitive tokens, appeal lies to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of service (amended Law of 21 June 1999). During the appeal the contested name may not be used; the founders may proceed with incorporation under an alternative pre-cleared name without prejudice to the appeal.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 180-191 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 2 September 2011 on the right of establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation including the Articles of Association (Statuts) and the RCS registration form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of an SARL is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash at incorporation; the paid-up capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution and released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BY UNANIMOUS RESOLUTION, the subscribers and founding board of the SARL hereby: (1) accept and record the subscription of 12,000 ordinary shares for an aggregate cash contribution of EUR 12,000, such shares being fully paid up upon contribution and deposit in the company's blocked account; (2) ratify the Articles of Association and fix the registered office at the address set out in the notarized deed, in the District of Luxembourg; (3) appoint [Manager Name] as Manager (Gérant) and sole officer, with exclusive authority to represent the company in all acts, sign filings, and obtain registrations; (4) authorize the Manager to procure the RCS filing, publication, and governmental permits, and to open the corporate bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Capital Deposit and Blocked Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, or Banque Raiffeisen)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate draft and KYC dossiers to a Luxembourg bank to open a blocked account in the future SARL's name. Transfer the EUR 12,000 minimum capital and obtain a blocked-funds certificate confirming that the funds are frozen until RCS registration and will only be available to the company after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Valid passport copies of all subscribers and proposed Manager
Anti-money laundering source-of-funds declaration
Beneficial owner identification form
Draft business plan and commercial substance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC or beneficial-ownership documentation, promptly supplement the requested source-of-funds evidence or open the blocked account with an alternate licensed credit institution, then reissue the blocked-funds certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary admitted to the Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary prepares, reads, and authenticates the deed of incorporation in Luxembourg. The subscribers sign in person or through a properly notarized power of attorney. The bank blocked-funds certificate must be presented to the notary, who verifies full subscription and payment of the share capital before signing the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Bank blocked-funds certificate
Identity documents of all shareholders and Manager
Proof of residential address of subscribers
Declaration of non-condemnation (Article 179 of the Commercial Companies Law)
Beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the corporate object, capital, or owner declarations, the parties must approve a rectification clause or restated statute, execute a supplemental notarized act, and proceed with the initial filing only after full cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Filing, Registration, and Company Number Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed electronically or physically with the RCS. Pay the prescribed registration fee, submit the declaration of officers and beneficial owners, and obtain the official RCS extract with the registration number. This step creates the legal personality of the SARL.
required_dossiers: Notarized original or certified copy of the Deed of Incorporation
Statement of non-condemnation of the Manager
Bank certificate certifying fully paid-up share capital
Copy of the Manager's and shareholders' identity documents
Beneficial ownership declaration for the RCS register
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the registration file, submit a rectification act before the notary or amend the beneficial-ownership declaration, and resubmit the corrected dossier within the RCS deadline; once corrected, the registration must proceed without further substantive review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Disclosure and Publication in the Official Electronic Collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) operated by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS acceptance, the publication of the deed is made automatically in the official electronic collection. Order certified copies of the publication and the RCS extract for use in bank account activation, commercial licensing, and customer due-diligence files.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
RCS-accepted incorporation deed
Articles of Association
List of officers and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, notify the LBR in writing, provide the notarially certified correct version, and request a rectification publication with retro-effect where permitted by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economy / General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment license application through the single point of submission (guichet.lu) for the wholesale beverage distribution and storage activities. The application must evidence the professional capacity and good conduct of the Manager and must be obtained before commencement of commercial operations.
required_dossiers: Completed application form on guichet.lu
Official RCS extract
Criminal record certificate (bulletin n°3) of the Manager
Proof of professional training or at least three years of relevant management experience
Lease agreement or property title for the registered premises
Tax and social security clearance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests further evidence or refuses the license, the applicant may file a formal administrative challenge or appeal within one month, submitting a supplemented professional-capacity and compliance folder before the Minister of the Economy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Brewery Excise, Food Hygiene, and Operational Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Douanes et Accises (Customs and Excise); Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA); Municipal Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an excise warehousekeeper for beer, file the food-safety and HACCP self-check notification with ALVA, and obtain any municipal environmental or physical-operation permit required for the microbrewery and cold-chain storage areas. The route is mandatory for production, storage, and wholesale distribution of craft beer.
required_dossiers: Site plan and sanitary file
HACCP food safety plan
Excise warehouse application form and capacity statement
Waste management and wastewater discharge agreement
Fire safety and occupational health preliminary file
Cold-chain equipment and refrigerant inventory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If excise or ALVA queries the application, submit the requested technical supplements within the reopened administrative period; where the denial is substantive, an appeal may be brought before the administrative court while re-engineering the HACCP and environmental plan with a licensed consulting engineer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy / General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship in coordination with the Customs and Excise Administration and the Luxembourg Environment Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Establishment License (Autorisation d'Établissement) for wholesale beer distribution and Excise Warehousekeeper Permit for beer production, storage, and dispatch

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Simplified assessment / environmental registration for a microbrewery below the annual production threshold; a full EIA report is not required where beer production capacity remains below 200,000 hectolitres per year.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to public sewer must comply with municipal sanitation limits and EU Urban Wastewater Directive standards: BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/l, COD ≤ 125 mg/l, total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/l, pH 6.5-9.5; refrigerant gases must be HFC/HCFC-free with leakage monitoring; spent grain and yeast must be recovered as waste code 02 03 04 under a licensed waste management plan; VOC and brewery odour emissions are controlled through local zoning and an odour management plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps and municipal fire-prevention inspection; structural load inspection certificates for tanks, keg racks, and cold-chain storage areas; occupational health and workplace clearance by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) covering forklift operations, pressurized keg handling, and low-temperature work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct and corporate income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties, and excise on beer; centralized business-tax filing portal at MyGuichet.lu; company legal-identity register: Registre de Commerce et des Societes (Luxembourg Business Registers, RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SARL in craft-beer distribution: (1) notarized incorporation, deposit of minimum capital with a Luxembourg bank, and filing of the articles with the RCS to obtain the national business registration number (numéro d'immatriculation / 'matricule'), which is the base legal identifier; (2) apply via MyGuichet.lu to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits) using the matricule and the standard VAT registration form; the VAT ID must be obtained before making any Luxembourg taxable supply, before intra-EU acquisitions, and before issuing zero-rated export invoices; (3) a non-EU-established entity must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) approved by the AEDT; an EU-established foreign parent generally files directly but may opt for a representative; (4) complete the beneficial-ownership (RBE) register filing and appoint local governance (at least one manager) before the tax ID is activated; the same matricule is used for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Luxembourg SARL is a civil-law corporate entity fully taxable at entity level as a Luxembourg tax resident on worldwide income, plus municipal business tax and net wealth tax; no pass-through or check-the-box transparency is recognized for income tax purposes; a pure distribution SARL without economic substance, premises, staff, and decision-making functions is at risk of being recharacterized as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent or as an artificial arrangement under GAAR/ATAD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg provides no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed by civil law. Available statutory elections affecting the SARL include: (i) corporate income-tax group election (régime d'intégration fiscale) for a Luxembourg parent holding at least 95% of sub-subsidiaries, elected for a 5-year term; (ii) participation exemption regime: election/qualification to exempt 100% of qualifying dividend income and capital gains (10% participation held for at least 12 months and subject to substance/compliance conditions); (iii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) pooling VAT registration of related Luxembourg entities; (iv) depreciation and asset revaluation elections under the Luxembourg income tax law (LIR); (v) hybrid-mismatch disclosure and election statements under ATAD to allocate deduction/inclusion outcomes; (vi) no transparency election is available for a SARL, which is always opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA) implemented under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC and the Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979, plus excise duty on beer under EU Directive 62/2020/EU administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small businesses (small-business exemption under Art. 57 of the VAT law; indexation adjusted to approximately EUR 35,000 from 1 January 2023, current figure to be verified); non-established foreign suppliers have zero registration threshold and must register for any Luxembourg taxable supply; a wholesaler dealing exclusively in zero-rated export supplies must still VAT-register to claim input VAT refunds; intra-EU distance-sale threshold is EUR 10,000 EU-wide, administered through the EU One-Stop-Shop.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), digital stamping, or mandatory B2B e-invoicing exists in Luxembourg for wholesale or export operations as of the current regime; mandatory structured e-invoicing (Peppol BIS 3.0) applies only for B2G supplies to Luxembourg public contracting authorities; all VAT returns, European Sales Lists (recapitulative statements), and Intrastat declarations are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu; export transactions are controlled through customs AES/SAD records rather than VAT invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT (0%) applies to: (i) export supplies of craft beer delivered outside the EU, provided physical departure from the EU is documented within 90 days of supply; (ii) intra-Community supplies of beer to a VAT-registered customer in another EU Member State, evidenced by the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, the commercial invoice statement 'exonération TVA / article 42 LTV', and the recapitulative statement (European Sales List); (iii) services directly connected with exported goods (e.g., internal transport and handling incidental to the export); (iv) deliveries to ships/aircraft on international routes under qualifying conditions; brewery cellar-door or on-premises sales in Luxembourg remain taxable at the applicable domestic VAT rate and must be separately invoiced from zero-rated export dispatches.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / AES electronic export record)
Bill of Lading (or CMR consignment note / air waybill for road and air export routes)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation evidencing receipt from the foreign buyer; Luxembourg banks issue payment confirmations rather than government certificates)
Commercial invoice with explicit zero-rating statement, reason code, and customer VAT/GIN details
Proof of dispatch or delivery (signed POD/customs seals) and, for intra-EU, the customer's valid EU VAT number and recapitulative statement entry
Intrastat dispatch declaration and European Sales List filing where statutory thresholds are exceeded
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT systematically audits export substantiation files for beer wholesalers; missing, contradictory, or late export evidence triggers immediate VAT re-credit at 17% (or the applicable reduced rate) with default interest at 3% per annum from the date the VAT fell due; administrative penalties for inaccurate or late declarations range from 25% up to 100% of the tax for concealment and from EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 for procedural breaches; intentional or fraudulent export zero-rating claims may trigger criminal tax-fraud prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 50,000, increased up to 10-20 years for organized or aggravated evasion; the VAT fiscal representative and responsible directors/managers are jointly and severally liable for clawed-back amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem alongside the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential regulation of credit institutions and payment services is jointly discharged by the BCL and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility. Luxembourg applies Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), guaranteeing unrestricted movement of capital between EU member states and third countries; no exchange control authorization is required for inbound equity injections, dividend distributions, or trade settlements. Profit remittance is impeded only by the statutory 15% dividend withholding tax, which is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) and to 5% under the Luxembourg tax treaties with Germany and the United States where the 10% shareholding threshold is met. Eurozone membership eliminates convertibility and transfer risk for euro-denominated treasury positions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio on export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in any currency in any jurisdiction; the only obligations are the general anti-money-laundering framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) and BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting for cross-border direct investment flows exceeding EUR 12,500.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account (compte de séquestre) for SARL formation
Operational Account; Trade Finance and Documentary Credit Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Luxembourg provides no standalone licensing gateway for offshore digital banks or non-EEA EMI brands; payment institutions must be authorized by the CSSF under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services (PSD2 transposition) to passport Luxembourg payment accounts. Offshore EMIs (UK, US, Singapore or Cyprus-licensed entities) cannot obtain a native LU IBAN, fall outside the CSSF resolution framework, and are rejected as a primary treasury rail for a cold-chain wholesaler. Their acceptable role is limited to ancillary collections, never for escrowed capital or tax-critical disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized signatory (the SARL gérant/manager) is effectively mandatory for the initial account opening with the four tier-1 banks; alternatively, a notarized power of attorney with apostille may be accepted, but this prolongs onboarding by 5-10 business days. Remote opening via eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures is technically permissible for EEA directors, but CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the amended AML Law of 12 November 2004 require an in-person interview for any non-EEA ultimate beneficial owner. The pragmatic path is a single-day physical visit to Luxembourg with the gérant and authorized UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain without demonstrable Luxembourg substance triggers the 'letterbox company' red flag under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and OECD BEPS considerations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts of Luxembourg-resident staff; social security registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); commercial lease agreement for warehouse/cold-storage premises; annual board minutes evidencing decisions taken in Luxembourg; substance opinion from Luxembourg counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity intercompany transfers and immediate outbound movement of funds from the capital escrow account after registration, assessed by the bank as potential money-muling or fictitious turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed distribution agreements with breweries; pro-forma invoices for keg purchases; 12-month cash-flow forecast reconciled to the trade mission; sworn declaration on the origin of the injected funds; notarized capital subscription voucher from the incorporation deed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alcoholic beverage distribution without the appropriate establishment authorization raises the 'unlicensed regulated activity' screening flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to professions; ALVA (Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire) food business operator registration; municipal alcohol sales and storage permit; sanitary certificates for the EU cold chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP database match: UBO holding a passport from a country with partial EU sanctions alignment, or beneficial owner name resembling a politically exposed person.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF-compliant sanctions self-certification; legal opinion on the UBO's full beneficial ownership history; official residency and citizenship certificates; source-of-wealth audit trail supported by tax returns and share purchase instruments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent company or subscriber executes an SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA SCT using an ISO 20022 pacs.008 message) to the blocked capital escrow account (compte de séquestre) held at the chosen Luxembourg credit institution in the name of the SARL en formation. The wire must carry SWIFT purpose code 'EQUI' (Equity-linked security/capital contribution) and reference 'Share capital contribution under Article 710-1 et seq. of the amended Law of 10 August 1915'. The notary certifies full subscription and payment of the minimum EUR 12,000 capital before the deed is filed with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). The bank blocks the funds until RCS registration; thereafter the escrow is converted into the operational account. The entity must report the inbound direct investment to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics whenever the receipt exceeds EUR 12,500. Charge 'SHA' is standard; if the full amount must land in escrow without deductions, charge 'OUR' must be selected explicitly.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for both EU and overseas brewery settlements, using charge 'SHA' and trade-related purpose codes ('GDDS' for goods or 'TRDP'). Secondary rail is a confirmed irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP 600, issued via SWIFT MT700) for keg shipments exceeding EUR 50,000, with bills of lading, commercial invoices, and ALVA sanitary certificates as presenting documents. For recurring EU supplier collections, the company deploys SEPA Direct Debit Core (scheme creditor identifier registered in Luxembourg) against the target rail 'Local_Direct_Debit'. All outbound disbursements above EUR 10,000 must be backed by contemporaneous trade documents (order, invoice, CMR/BOL, customs entry) to prevent AML friction; cold-chain logistics documents also mitigate scrutiny of alcohol cross-border traffic.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP; maturities up to 12 months) executed with the Luxembourg relationship bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a local master agreement
FX Swaps and rollover forwards for managing commercial liquidity mismatches between EUR receipts and USD/GBP brewery payables
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on illiquid non-EMU brewing-input currencies (BRL, MXN, ZAR, AUD) settled in cash in EUR
European-style purchased FX options (zero-premium and plain-vanilla) used exclusively to cap import costs without speculative leverage
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) aligned with the long-term USD trade finance facility for large-capital keg import programs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) deposit with the register of commerce, in full or abridged format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), via the eJustice electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within 6 months after balance sheet date; filing with RCS due within 1 month after approval and in any case within 7 months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end the filing must be completed by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal notice from the RCS, administrative fines up to EUR 1,250, and possible further action by the Public Prosecutor seeking judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS in case of persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (confirmation annuelle) in the UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), via the RBE e-file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory at least once each calendar year; the confirming return must be filed within 12 months after the most recent UBO declaration or confirmation (anniversary-based deadline).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Law of 13 January 2019 may lead to criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment of managers for deliberate breach; repeated failure may also escalate to administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, municipal business tax return, and net wealth tax return package (Forms 1002, 1007 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg direct tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the filing is due by 30 June of the following year; the tax administration normally grants an automatic extension to 31 December when filed through certified tax professionals.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of up to 10% of the assessed tax due (minimum EUR 25), late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, and, in aggravated cases, administrative fines and criminal prosecution of the managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Re-appointment of the independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) by the annual general meeting, where annual accounts are subject to statutory audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing is required; the appointment is recorded in the minute book and reflected in the statutory registers and annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting approving the annual accounts is held within 6 months after the financial year-end; the auditor's mandate covers the financial year and is subject to re-appointment at the general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a required auditor may trigger a court-initiated designation, civil liability of the gérants for failure to appoint, rejection of the statutory accounts filing, and referral to the Public Prosecutor by the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is required to appoint an independent auditor when it exceeds, for two consecutive financial years, at least two of the following thresholds: balance sheet total greater than EUR 4,400,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees greater than 50. If these thresholds are not exceeded, the SARL is exempt from mandatory audit and may file abridged annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and applicable EU accounting directives, primarily EU Directive 2013/34/EU. IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts; for a standalone SARL, Luxembourg GAAP remains the default statutory accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each entity must file an annual confirmation with the RBE, calculated by adding 12 months to the date of the most recent UBO filing or confirmation. The confirmation re-verifies the shareholding data already on record. Any material change in ownership, including a transfer of SARL shares, requires a new updated UBO declaration to be filed within one month of the share register update; the annual confirmation is not a substitute for this event-driven return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members (shareholders) with history of transfers, pledges and usufruct
Register of directors and managers (gérants) and statutory representatives
Minute book of general meetings and managing partner resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - USD 2,700 (approximately EUR 1,000 - EUR 2,500) per annum for registered office, domiciliation, corporate secretarial, RBE/RCS filing and annual maintenance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 16,000 (approximately EUR 5,500 - EUR 15,000) per annum for an independent statutory audit by an approved cabinet de révision agréé when the audit threshold is exceeded
